World & measurement rules

The 5,044 catalogue directions are paired with deterministic synthetic depths of 6–18 light-years. Every catalogue star is eligible as a spawn anchor. This is a game world, not real interstellar navigation. An ideal synthetic scan reads catalogue tags, ranges, and ship-frame bearings. Four noncoplanar ranges recover position; bearings recover orientation; four further landmarks test the solution. Residuals describe numerical agreement, not real sensor accuracy.

A softened local attraction acts around the starting star. Gravity suppression sets its force multiplier to zero for the remaining lifetime (at most 1,000 simulated years), costing 6 fuel. An impulse changes velocity and costs 250 fuel per light-year/year of velocity change; braking follows the same rule. Once suppressed, coast motion is force-free. The asteroid is stationary, with a 100 km radius, a schematic marker, a 0.003 ly game operation region and one finite deposit; extraction costs 3 fuel, 2 credits, and 2 years, yielding at most 32 fuel and 8 credits. There is no storage cap. Arrival requires a distance below 0.002 light-years and relative speed below 0.00001 light-years/year.

Astra credits and delegation are fictional game resources. Live Astra uses the existing local Codex bridge; unavailable calls pause the game and consume no fictional credits. Previews and conversations do not advance time. This journey is held in memory; New sky starts a fresh one.

A long journey, made together.
